SPECIFICATION FOR CARPET YARN MADE FROM VIRGIN WOOL

0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 10 February 1984, after the draft finalized by the Wool and Wool Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Par the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE details and 1.1 This standard prescribes the manufacturing requirements of wool yarn used for the piles or tufts of carpets. 2. MANUFACTURE 2.1 The yarn shall be evenly spun from virgin wool having minimum fibre length of 45 mm and of hairiness grade III or better and fineness grade D or better as per IS : 10930-1984t, and fully scoured. 3. TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Wool Yarn Woollen, semi-worsted or worsted spun yarn. Number of 1 000-m hanks in, one kilogram. other

5. PACKING 5.1 The carpet yarn may be supplied in hanks, cones or cheeses as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. The yarn shall be packed in accordance with the method given in IS : 32-1971* or IS : 741-1971t as the case may be. 6. MARKING 6.1 Each hank, cone or cheese and bale or case of the carpet yarn shall be marked with the following: a) Description of yarn, that is, `carpet yarn made from virgin wool'; b) Count of yarn; c) Name, initials or trade-mark d) Net mass of the package; e) Month and year of manufacture; and for Moth-Resistance'. f) If desired by the buyer, the words `Treated of the manufacturer, if any;

*Code for seaworthy packaging of woollen and worsted yarn and cloth ( second fetiion ) . *Code for inland packaging of woollen and worsted yarn and cloth (/irst reuisioa ).

5

is t 10921

l

1984

6.1.1 Each hank, cone of cheese and bale or case may also be marked with the IS1 Certificatioh Mark.
NOTE - The use of the IS1 CertiIication Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirementa of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and qualitv control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

7. SAMPLING

AND CRITERION

FOR

CONFORMITY

7.1 Lot - The quantity of the carpet yarn of the same count and composition, manufactured from the same quality of raw wool and delivered to the buyer against one despatch note shall constitute a lot. 7.2 The conformity of a lot to the requirements of this standar,d determined on the basis of the test results obtained on the samples from the lot. Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer seller, the number of bales or cases to be selected at random for the sample packages shall be as follows: No. of Bales or Cases in the Lot
up to 15

shall be selected and the drawing

No. of Bales or Cases to be Stlected

2
3 5' 8

16to 25
26 to 100 101 and above

7.3 The number of packages to be drawn from each bale or case selected according to 7.2 shall be 5. The number of test specimens to be prepared from each package shall be such that at least 20 test specimens are available for carrying out the tests for count, fibre length, fibre fineness and twist. A composite sample shall be prepared out of the test specimens and the same shall be tested for wool content, extractable matter, invoice mass and colour fastness ( for dyed yarn ). 7.4 Criterion for Conformity - The lot shall be considered as conforming to this standard if all thetest results satisfy the requirements laid down in Table 1.

A-i. TEST SAMPLRS
A-l.1 Knit or weave into fabric the composite sample [ sri 7.3 ) of the carpet yarn, and draw from it two test pieces; e&h hot &ss tlian 14 x 5 cm. Altetiatimly; prepare two test piee;ts ii-1the form of a layer of parallel stran,ds of yarns by wrapping the yarn lengthwise on a rectangular cardboard of size not smaller than 14 x 5 cm. A-2. APPARATUS A-2.1 Suitable Testing Device - An apparatus equipped &ith a fin&& of 1.6 cm diameter capable to move.to and fro in a straight line along a IO-cm track on the specimen with a downward force of 9 N.
NOTE - A suitable apparatus is the Crockmrter, described in the Technical Manual of the American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists ( Vol50, 1974 P 112 ).

A-2.2 Undyed Cloth undyed wool cloth. A-3. PROCEDURE A-3.1 Dry Rubbing

Adequate number of pieces, each 5 x 5 cm, of

Fix a A-3.1.1 Take one test piece and fix it to the rubbing device. piece of the dry undyed wool cloth in place over the end of the finger of rubbing device and rub it to and fro in a straight line along a track 10 cm long on the ( dry ) test piece 10 times in 10 seconds with a downward force of 9 N on the finger. A-3.1.2 Treat the second test piece in a similar manner using a fresh piece of undyed wool cloth. A-3.1.3 Evaluate by the method prescribed in IS : 769-1956* the degree of staining of that piece of undyed wool cloth which shows heavier staining. A-3.2 Wet Rubbing

A-3.2.1 Take a fresh ( dry ) test' piece and fix it to the rubbing device. Soak a fresh piece of undyed cloth in a solution of sodium hypochlorite having 2.5 g/l available chlorine and 30.8 g/l sodium hydroxide at 25�C and then squeeze so that it contains its own mass of liquor ( see Note ).
*Method of evaluating staining.

7

IS : 10921- 1984 Fix it in place over the end of the finger of the testing device and rub it to and fro in a straight line along a track 10 cm long on the ( dry ) test piece 10 times in 10 seconds with a downward force of 9 N on the finger. Dry the piece at room temperature.
NOTE-When the piece is to be wetted to contain its own mass of sodium hypochlorite solution, it may be saturated with the solution and then drawn between two rubber rollers, squeezed by means of a rubber roller on a glass plate or centrifuged. Wringing by hand does not give uniform wetting.

A-3.2.2 Treat the second test piece in a similar manner using piece of undyed wool cloth, and dry it at room temperature.
